outcome: use of non-pharmacological methods for pain relief
timely clamping of the umbilical cord
cohort: The study included 1,442 parturient women at usual risk who delivered in a maternity hospital in Northeastern Brazil between January 2020 and December 2021.
finding: Women who had normal deliveries were significantly more likely to experience good delivery and birth practices recommended by the World Health Organization.
mod_finding: Women with normal deliveries were 3.95 times more likely to have skin-to-skin contact, 13.2 times more likely to use non-pharmacological pain relief methods, 1.7 times more likely to have a companion, and 1.6 times more likely to have timely umbilical cord clamping compared to those who underwent cesarean sections.
